recommendation: Keep this no-change audit for FHIR-36334. Any remaining broad cleanup for examples, explicit return types/cardinalities, or error-handling consistency on newer FHIRPath functions should be handled under the later R6 issues after final work-group disposition.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-core R5 clarification asking that FHIR-defined FHIRPath functions define behavior for input collections with more than one element, specifically identifying hasValue(), getValue(), memberOf(), subsumes(), subsumedBy(), htmlChecks, and ofType().
initial_application: Git commit b97b828202710802aebb6b743dc18ac3fba16cc1 explicitly implemented FHIR-36334 in source/fhirpath.html by adding singleton, empty-input, and collection behavior to the named FHIRPath functions. The current source still contains those applied semantics, with later editorial refinements.
additional_context: The originating Zulip thread confirms the concern that singleton functions should document repeating-input behavior, and FHIR-I WGM 202205 minutes record a 15-0-0 Persuasive motion for FHIR-36334. FHIR-36335 is the related FHIRPath-spec companion issue handled by ITS. Later R6 tickets FHIR-53951 and FHIR-53960 raise broader examples, type/cardinality, and error-handling cleanup for newer FHIRPath content, but they are Triaged/not final and were not reconciled here.
reconciliation: No source change was made. publish.ini includes fhirpath.html in build scope, and source/fhirpath.html currently defines the requested cardinality behavior for the FHIR-36334 function set: hasValue()/getValue() require a single FHIR primitive or return empty, ofType() works across the input collection, memberOf()/subsumes()/subsumedBy() define singleton input and parameter behavior, and htmlChecks returns empty when invoked on a collection.

R6 Triaged issue about inconsistent FHIRPath error handling and weight() cardinality; not final and not part of this R5 audit.
